summary: The fallback clock assigns the same 0.0-minute duration to each compute-bound entry, so it cannot rank them or attribute phase costs. The locked GPU classification indicates no idle defect during compute work; the snapshot instead shows one device doing work while the other can accept a separate task.
bottlenecks_identified: Modification timestamps collapse the milestone to a shared 0.0-minute reading, which removes the detail needed for causal performance analysis.
Receipts omit task phases, accelerator activity, batch size, model concurrency, and runner choice; this prevents attribution and a runner audit.
The monitor saw only one Python inference process; the supplied timing cannot show whether request batching would reduce elapsed time.
improvements_suggested: Write monotonic task start, task end, and phase timestamps instead of relying on disk modification times.
Add task-scoped accelerator samples, model count, batch size, and runner choice to each execution receipt.
Schedule separate compute-bound experiments across available GPUs when the tasks are independent and each model fits on one device.
Batch multiple questions per forward pass on single-process inference paths.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Replace disk-mtime timing fallback with task-scoped monotonic phase receipts.
Add GPU-aware scheduling for independent compute-bound experiments.
Batch inference requests and record the batch size in the task receipt.
meta_reflection: With no elapsed minutes recorded, any positive savings percentage would be invented. The blocks do not say that multiple models ran together, so they cannot reveal a DualGPURunner miss.
